dis.mod.cardiac.name: Cardiac
dis.mod.cardiac.about: Heart rate and blood pressure compared with your usual ranges.
dis.steps.cardiac.1: Keep a regular log of blood pressure readings to show your doctor.
dis.steps.cardiac.2: Ask your doctor how often your heart should be checked.
dis.steps.cardiac.3: Bring your medicine list to every visit.
dis.mod.neuro.name: Neurological
dis.mod.neuro.about: No live readings in this prototype; reports and notes only.
dis.steps.neuro.1: Note any new headaches, weakness or speech changes and when they happened.
dis.steps.neuro.2: Ask your doctor which scans or tests suit you.
dis.mod.respiratory.name: Respiratory
dis.mod.respiratory.about: Oxygen level (SpO2) compared with your usual range.
dis.steps.respiratory.1: Note when breathing feels harder and what you were doing.
dis.steps.respiratory.2: Ask your doctor about a lung check if you have a cough that lasts.
dis.steps.respiratory.3: Keep your inhaler or medicines where you can reach them.
dis.mod.diabetes.name: Diabetes
dis.mod.diabetes.about: Glucose readings compared with your usual range.
dis.steps.diabetes.1: Note glucose readings with meal times to share with your doctor.
dis.steps.diabetes.2: Ask your doctor how often to test and what range is right for you.
dis.mod.kidney.name: Kidney
dis.mod.kidney.about: No live readings in this prototype; reports and notes only.
dis.steps.kidney.1: Keep recent kidney test reports (creatinine, eGFR) together.
dis.steps.kidney.2: Ask your doctor how often these tests are needed.
dis.steps.kidney.3: Tell every doctor about all medicines you take.
dis.mod.liver.name: Liver
dis.mod.liver.about: No live readings in this prototype; reports and notes only.
dis.steps.liver.1: Keep recent liver test reports together.
dis.steps.liver.2: Ask your doctor how often these tests are needed.
dis.steps.liver.3: Tell every doctor about all medicines and supplements you take.

ri.intro: Add values from your medical reports. They update your Twin only after you confirm them.
ri.honest: This prototype cannot read your files by itself. Read the number from your report and type it in. Nothing reaches your Twin until you confirm it, and no clinician has reviewed it.
ri.add: Add a value from a report
ri.low: Lowest value printed on the report (optional)
ri.high: Highest value printed on the report (optional)
ri.rangeHelp: Type the range printed on your own report if there is one. The app does not decide what is normal.
ri.confirmText: Compare it with your report. It is added to your Twin only when you press Confirm.
ri.confirm: Confirm and add to my Twin
ri.saveError: Could not save on this device. Storage may be blocked.
ri.noneConfirmed: You have not confirmed any values yet.
ri.deviceOnly: Saved only on this device for now. They are not sent to the hospital.
ri.status.within: Inside the range on your report
ri.status.outside: Outside the range on your report
ri.err.order: The highest value must not be below the lowest.
ri.err.future: The date cannot be in the future.
sim.intro: Try a "what if" value and see where it would sit compared with your own usual range.
sim.notPrediction: This is a what-if tool. It does not predict what will happen, does not estimate any risk and is not a diagnosis. It only compares a number you choose with your own usual range.
sim.summaryIn: With these values, nothing would be outside your usual range.
sim.summaryOut: With these values, these would be outside your usual range: {{names}}. This says nothing about what would actually happen.
sim.assume.1: The baseline is your latest shared reading. With no reading yet, the sliders start in the middle of your usual range.
sim.assume.2: "Usual range" is the range saved in your profile. The app does not know what is normal for anyone else.
sim.assume.3: Each value is looked at on its own. Combinations and effects on each other are not modelled.
sim.assume.4: No medicines, activity, sleep or illness are taken into account.
sim.uncertaintyHelp: Your real readings move around from moment to moment. A what-if inside this spread is not unusual for you.

about.title: About the 3D body
about.intro: Where the body model comes from and what it can and cannot show.
about.attribution: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC Attribution 4.0 International.
about.changes: Changes made here: only some parts kept, simplified and compressed, organs merged into named parts, colours chosen by us.
about.lungs: The lung shapes are a generic outline drawn round each lung's airway tree, because the source has no solid lung surface.
about.generic: It is a generic adult male reference body, not a scan of you.
about.notDiagnosis: It never diagnoses. Colours and words such as "may need attention" only compare simulated readings with your usual range.
about.simulated: All readings are simulated. This is a prototype and not a medical device.
crumb.label: You are here
hero.label: Welcome

footer.notice: Simulated demo. Not medical advice. Not a medical device.
footer.team: HealthTwin AI is a student prototype by Jehal, Puneet and Daksh. All data is simulated.
about.acc1: Every page works with a keyboard and a screen reader, and text meets WCAG AA contrast in the light and dark themes.
about.acc2: Motion stops when your device asks for less motion, and the 3D body has a list and a text label as an alternative.
about.acc3: The app is checked automatically with axe-core in English, Hindi and Gujarati. Hindi and Gujarati text are drafts and have not yet been reviewed by native speakers.
